title: Jurisdiction-aware compliance intake router with automated redline suggestions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise sales and legal teams are submitting compliance asks (DPA, GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2 questionnaires) where the required response path depends on account region, hosting mode (hosted/dedicated/private), and data residency constraints. Current intake routes items to a human queue which causes 48-72h triage delays and repeated evidence requests.

Proposal: Build a Jurisdiction-Aware Compliance Intake Router that programmatically classifies incoming asks by jurisdiction, hosting sensitivity, and control surface. The router will attach a prioritized response lane (fast-path, standard, legal-review), auto-tag required evidence templates, and surface automated redline suggestions for common DPA clauses using a curated clause library. Integrations: Slack/Email intake, GA ticket creation, GitHub links, and Drive/Confluence artifacts.

Scope: In-scope for MVP: jurisdiction detection (EU/US/APAC + extra countries), hosting-mode qualifier, evidence template attachment, lane assignment automation, redline suggestion engine with editable suggestions (no auto-apply), and dashboard metrics for time-to-triage and SLA adherence. Out-of-scope: fully automated DPA signing, legal approval automation, and on-prem agent for air-gapped intake (later phase).
acceptance_criteria: 1) New incoming compliance ticket is assigned a jurisdiction tag with >=92% accuracy on the evaluation set. 2) Tickets are auto-assigned to a response lane (fast-path/standard/legal) based on configurable rules and account metadata. 3) Evidence bundle suggestions appear in the ticket with links to templates and a confidence score. 4) Redline suggestion panel surfaces up to 5 prioritized clause edits and links to supporting rationale. 5) Dashboard shows a reduction in median triage time from 48h to <=8h for fast-path items in the pilot accounts.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (Pilot): Internal legal + 3 enterprise pilot customers, feature-flagged intake in PROD; 2-week observation.
Phase 1: Open to all accounts with hosted/dedicated hosting; add automated SLA notifications and Slack workflow.
Phase 2: Add APAC jurisdiction refinement, account-level overrides, and LLM-assisted evidence summarization.
Fallback policy: If confidence < 0.5 or ticket has free-text escalation markers, route to 'legal review' lane and include suggested tags for human reviewer.
risks: Misclassification of jurisdiction could cause regulatory non-compliance
Over-reliance on suggested redlines without legal review
Data residency metadata may be incomplete for older accounts
implementation_notes:
- Use existing account metadata service + geolocation heuristics for jurisdiction inference.
- Start with rule-based routing augmented by a small supervised classifier trained on historical intake tickets.
- Redline suggestions implemented as 'diff candidates' from clause library; show provenance and confidence.
- Store evidence templates in a read-only Drive folder and link to them in tickets.
- Telemetry: tokenized reasons for lane decision, classifier confidence, evidence attached, time-to-first-action.
- Ensure PII free paths when sending content to any LLM service; use redacted text for suggestion generation.
